source_title: Mpac Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 58 that the financial statements were approved by the Directors on 3 March 2020; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Mpac reported a transformational 2019: order intake increased 37% to £87.6m, revenue increased 52% to £88.8m, underlying operating profit increased to £7.7m from £1.4m and return on sales rose to 8.7%. Cash fell to £18.9m from £27.9m, principally after the Lambert acquisition and associated working-capital use, while operating cash inflow before reorganisation improved to £5.1m. A limited restructuring of the UK head office and Coventry site and Lambert integration actions were undertaken during the year.
already_announced_exclusion: The UK head-office and Coventry restructuring, Lambert integration actions and related reorganisation payments were undertaken before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event; ordinary One Mpac integration and efficiency activity is also excluded.
review_note: The acquisition-related cash reduction is contained and does not outweigh exceptional order, revenue, profit and margin growth; identified restructuring actions were already undertaken and excluded.

source_title: Mpac Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 25, 46 and 63 that the Strategic Report, responsibility statement and financial statements were approved by the Board or Directors on 16 March 2022; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Global supply-chain and resource constraints, materials-price increases and COVID-related labour availability affected operations, but Mpac reported minimal disruption. Order intake increased 40% to £117.9m, revenue increased to £94.3m, underlying profit before tax increased to £8.6m and return on sales improved. Cash reduced slightly to £14.5m and operating cash inflow before reorganisation fell to £0.8m after an £8.2m working-capital increase, but the £10m revolving facility remained undrawn and net assets rose to £65.4m.
already_announced_exclusion: The Switchback integration and prior reorganisation costs were already undertaken or recognised before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event; ordinary brand alignment, operational-efficiency and growth initiatives are also excluded.
review_note: Supply, price, labour and working-capital pressure is explicit but contained; order, revenue, profit, return-on-sales and net-asset growth plus an undrawn facility provide dominant quantified offsets.

source_title: Mpac Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 23, 48 and 61 that the Strategic Report, responsibility statement and financial statements were approved by the Board or Directors on 18 or 19 March 2024; the later Board approval date is used conservatively and the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Mpac recovered strongly from prior-year supply disruption: order intake increased 41% to a record £118.5m, revenue increased 17% to £114.2m, underlying operating profit doubled to £7.8m and the closing order book increased to £72.5m. Margins normalised through the year, operating cash inflow before reorganisation improved to £13.1m from a £12.8m outflow and the Group moved from £4.7m net debt to £2.1m net cash. Reorganisation costs of £1.2m were recognised and £0.8m paid during 2023.
already_announced_exclusion: The 2023 reorganisation costs and actions were already incurred or recognised before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event; ordinary strategic planning, ERP rollout, operational excellence and capacity investment are also excluded.
review_note: No unresolved company-level intervention pressure was identified: record orders, double-digit revenue growth, doubled profit, margin normalisation, strong cash conversion and net cash provide dominant contrary evidence.
